_note: The economy around Overthought & Co. Monthly figures move as seeded mean-reverting processes from the starting values below. Every starting value and anchor is an ASSUMPTION written from memory of recent UK figures, not checked against the source; the source to check is named beside it. Simulated figures are evidence about this world only, never a forecast of the real one.

consumer_confidence.unit: index (0 = as many feel better as worse)

bank_rate.check: Bank of England, Bank Rate history

wage_growth.check: ONS, Average weekly earnings, regular pay growth

history_anchors._note: Points the five-year history passes through (one per year, October figures), joined by a seeded wobbly line. ASSUMPTIONS from memory of UK figures; check each against the sources named in start.

processes._note: Each month: next = now + reversion x (long-run - now) + noise. Long-run values and speeds are assumptions chosen so figures drift back towards normal over a few years, as they tend to.

effects._note: How the figures reach the shop, each measured against the starting value (so an unchanged economy changes nothing). Sizes are assumptions picked to be modest: a novelty gift shop sells things nobody needs, so confidence matters, but a month's figures move it by a few per cent at most.
